title: End-to-End Google Earth Engine (Full Course)
language: English (course material and videos in English; no Russian version)
cost: Self-study (OpenCourseWare): free. Live instructor-led cohort: USD $229 / INR ₹15,999 + GST.
certificate: No certificate for the free self-study version. Employer-verifiable certificate issued ONLY for the paid live online classes upon completing all sessions and assignments.
duration: 27 hours of content. As a live cohort, typically conducted in 9 sessions of 3 hours each over 3 weeks. Self-study version is untimed/self-paced.
level: Beginner to Advanced (progresses from "Hello World" basics through ML classification, change detection, app building, and the Python API).
target_audience: GIS/remote-sensing practitioners, researchers and environmental analysts who want practical skills to implement remote-sensing workflows on cloud-based satellite imagery. Assumes basic GIS familiarity; no prior programming required (starts from Hello World). No specific agro/SMB focus.
format: Primarily self-paced OpenCourseWare: pre-recorded video lectures (YouTube playlist + downloadable Vimeo) plus a shared Earth Engine code repository of scripts/exercises added to your own GEE account. A paid live webinar/cohort variant (9 x 3h sessions over 3 weeks) is also offered with instructor support.
assessment: Per-module assignments; certificate gated behind paid live cohort; free version is self-checked/ungraded.
hands_on: Heavily hands-on. Every concept has an in-line "[Try in Code Editor]" interactive task. Course material is distributed as runnable GEE scripts in a shared code repository. 5 end-to-end Guided Projects on real scenarios: rainfall deviation, flood mapping, time-series extraction, landcover analysis, nighttime lights. Module 6 moves the same work into Python via Colab and QGIS.
tools: Google Earth Engine (JavaScript Code Editor — primary), Earth Engine Python API + Google Colab (Module 6), QGIS via the GEE plugin, XArray for Python data handling. Datasets: Sentinel-2 (and Sentinel-1, Landsat, MODIS), VIIRS DNB Nighttime Lights, TerraClimate, Dynamic World, Google CLOUD_SCORE_PLUS (cloud masking), GOOGLE/SATELLITE_EMBEDDING/V1/ANNUAL (deep-learning embeddings), ALOS World 3D DEM, GAUL admin boundaries, GHS Urban Centre Database. No SMAP observed.

syllabus.topics: 01 Hello World; 02 Working with Image Collections; 03 Filtering Image Collections; 04 Creating Mosaics and Composites from ImageCollections; 05 Working with Feature Collections; 06 Importing Data; 07 Clipping Images; 08 Exporting Data; Assignment 1
01 Earth Engine Objects; 02 Calculating Indices; 03 Computation on ImageCollections; 04 Cloud Masking; 05 Reducers; 06 Time-Series Charts; Assignment 2

Intro to Machine Learning & Supervised Classification; 01 Basic Supervised Classification; 02 Accuracy Assessment; 03 Feature Engineering; 04 Using Satellite Embeddings; 05 Exporting Classification Results; 06 Visualize Exported Images; 07 Calculating Area; Assignment 3
Intro to Change Detection; 01 Spectral Index Change; 02 Spectral Distance Change; 03 Direct Classification of Change; 04 Post-classification Comparison
01 Client vs. Server; 02 Using UI Elements; 03 Building and Publishing an App; 04 Publishing the App; 05 Create a Split Panel App

syllabus.module: Module 6 — Google Earth Engine Python API
syllabus.topics: Intro to Python API; 01 Python API Syntax; 02 Automatic Conversion of JavaScript Code to Python; 03 Batch Exports; 04 Using Earth Engine with XArray; 05 Automating Downloads; 06 Automating Exports; 07 Using the GEE QGIS Plugin
5 Guided Projects: rainfall deviation, flood mapping, time-series extraction, landcover analysis, nighttime lights; plus Learning Resources, Debugging and Scaling guidance

strengths: Truly $0 self-study path — full 27h of material, videos (YouTube + downloadable Vimeo) and a runnable code repository, all free; matches the FOLUR no-cost stack
Exercise design is exemplary: every single concept has an inline '[Try in Code Editor]' task, so learners never just watch — they run code immediately
End-to-end real-world Guided Projects (flood mapping, rainfall deviation, landcover, nighttime lights) connect primitives to a complete workflow, not toy snippets
Strong, modern dataset and technique choices: Dynamic World, Cloud Score+, deep-learning Satellite Embeddings, accuracy assessment, scaling to large regions
Covers the full pipeline incl. app-building (sharing results with non-coders) and a dedicated Python/Colab/QGIS module — directly mirrors the FOLUR Python+QGIS+GEE+Colab stack
Code distributed as a shareable GEE script repository you add to your own account — instantly reproducible, a clean model for hands-on delivery
weaknesses: English only — no Russian, so directly unusable for the Russian-language FOLUR audience without translation
Free version has no certificate and no autograded assessment; certification is paywalled behind the $229 live cohort
Audience is general GIS/RS practitioners, not agronomy/SMB; no farm-economics, agronomic interpretation, or business framing
Examples are global, not regional — nothing for North Kazakhstan (СКО/Костанай/Акмола); FOLUR must localize all AOIs and datasets
JavaScript-first; Python only arrives in Module 6, whereas FOLUR's stack is Python+Colob-centric from the start
No SMAP / soil-moisture or dedicated agricultural-monitoring track; emphasis is generic classification and change detection
